newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea says South blocking inter-Korean food aid.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says South blocking inter-Korean food aid.

text.p: North Korea on Tuesday accused the the South Korean government of blocking aid from civic and religious organisations to its starving people.

South Korean security authorities' insistence that private aid to the North go through official channels was "throwing a chill over the assistance to the North", the Korean Religionists Council said in a statement carried on the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) and monitored in Tokyo.
The statement also blasted the South Korean Red Cross for refusing to specify what amounts of aid it would offer the North at talks in Beijing on May 3 that ended without agreement.
"South Korea's Red Cross participated without preparations in the contact between the inter-Korean Red Cross working-level delegates in Beijing," said the statement.
It said the South's Red Cross was trying to control private aid to the North.
"If they are sincerely concerned about the misfortune of fellow countrymen and want to help them, they must give priority to the kinds and quantity of relief goods, not to procedures."
The South Korean Red Cross said it was unable to specify aid amounts until donations from South Korean charities were collected and counted.
North Korea was devastated by unprecedented floods in 1995 and again in 1996, which devastated crops and caused food shortages that hunger experts say could lead to widespread famine later this year.

The U.N. World Food Programme estimates North Korea needs 1.3 million tonnes of food to meet its basic needs in 1997. It has appealed for 200,000 tonnes of food worth $96 million, but has received only $38 million to date.
South Korea has pledged to give the rival North $6.0 million through the WFP this year, while the United States has offered $25.0 million.
